name: Cortés and the fall of Tenochtitlan
traveler: Hernán Cortés, Malintzin and their Tlaxcalan allies
summary: A few hundred Spaniards land on the Gulf coast, gain thousands of Indigenous allies who resent Mexica rule, and march on Tenochtitlan. With smallpox spreading ahead of them, they destroy the city after a long siege. Cortés's letters to Charles V put Mexico on Europe's map.

stops.note: Cortés sails against the governor's orders with eleven ships.
Finds Gerónimo de Aguilar, a shipwrecked Spaniard who speaks Maya.
After a battle, Malintzin is given to the Spaniards; speaking Nahuatl and Maya, she becomes the indispensable interpreter.

stops.place: Villa Rica de la Vera Cruz
stops.note: Founds a town to claim authority from the Crown and scuttles his ships.
After fierce fighting, the Tlaxcalans, enemies of the Mexica, become allies.
A massacre of the city's people.
Moctezuma receives them in a city of perhaps 200,000 on its lake.
Driven out on the Noche Triste, the Spaniards retreat to their allies. Smallpox spreads through Mexico.
After a 75-day siege the city falls and is razed; Mexico City is built on its ruins.

informs.note: Cortés's letters to Charles V, printed from 1522
